lessons.title: Fretboard map 1
lessons.focus: Natural notes on low E and A
learningObjectives: Explain or demonstrate the main idea: natural notes on low e and a.
Perform the target task accurately at a comfortable, controlled tempo.
Apply the skill in a short musical context and identify one next improvement.

explanation.keyIdea: The fretboard is a repeating pitch map. Each adjacent fret is one semitone. The natural-note sequence repeats A–G; B–C and E–F are adjacent semitones. Octave shapes connect the same note name in different positions.
explanation.plainLanguage: This lesson focuses on natural notes on low e and a. First understand the sound or movement, then practise a small part, then return to the musical whole. Treat the written checkpoint as an observable target, not a deadline.
explanation.workedExample: Low E/A note map, 2 minutes daily

demonstrationOrReference.referenceSuggestion: Use a clear, slow demonstration of natural notes on low e and a from a reputable guitar-learning source or your own view of the fretboard. Compare the demonstration with the step-by-step guide here; no paid-course video or protected tab is reproduced.
steps: Start from a known open-string note and move one fret at a time, naming each semitone.
Use the natural-note sequence A, B, C, D, E, F, G, remembering B–C and E–F have no intervening natural note.
Find the same note on another string using an octave relationship, then verify the pitch.
